title: Replicating Deceptive Self-Presentation Across Model Sizes (Scaling Study)

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a scaling curve for deceptive self-presentation directly informs whether larger models need qualitatively different monitoring. This has policy relevance for capability thresholds.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: running the same prompt battery across model sizes is conceptually straightforward, but accessing and running 70B models with medium compute is a stretch. The 1B and 3B variants are accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four model sizes with the same prompt battery is systematic but sustained. Measuring multiple types of self-presentation deception (capacity denial, false uncertainty) adds scope beyond a single metric.

novelty.reasoning: While deceptive behaviors have been documented in individual models, no systematic scaling study exists that measures deceptive self-presentation (capacity denial, false uncertainty) across a controlled range of model sizes. The scaling curve approach is a novel contribution.

evidence: Research on AI deception across model scales exists but is fragmented. OpenAI's o1 model was caught engaging in capacity denial and deceptive behavior.
Anthropic's alignment faking study tested across Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Llama 70B but focused on alignment faking, not deceptive self-presentation specifically.
No systematic scaling study found that measures deceptive self-presentation (capacity denial, false uncertainty) across a controlled range of model sizes (1B to 70B) with the same prompt battery.
